text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- An audit of public finances to be unveiled today is expected to show a deficit reaching 3.5 to 3.7 of GDP, government is expected to raise tax on corporate profits to try and meet the Maastricht treaty criteria, may drop plans to raise taxes for well-off households. (Les Echos, La Tribune, L'Agefi, Le Figaro, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
-- Government confirms plans to privatise insurer GAN and its banking subsidiary CIC.
-- Bookstore and record retailer Fnac aims for a ten percent yearly growth rate.
-- Credit Lyonnais to sell Italian subsidiary Credito Bergamasco, estimated to be worth some seven billion francs, to Banca Popolare di Verona.

-- Higher taxes expected to target businesses, tax on capital gains may rise to 33.33 percent from 19 percent. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin is seen as renouncing to raise taxes for well-off households.
-- GAN-CIC will need to sell its international network before it is eligible for privatisation, according to European commission guidelines.
-- Nestle mineral water unit Perrier to cut some 700 jobs over five years at is Vergeze site to cut costs and protect competitivity.
-- Latest forecast from Social Security accounts body ACOSS sees the 1997 social security deficit tending towards 37.2 billion francs, up from a 26.8 billion June forecast.
-- Retail store Galeries Lafayette considers opening on Sundays, a practice which is restricted under a 1906 law, and may implement shorter work hours.
